slides.title: What Is LINQ?
slides.content: LINQ (Language Integrated Query) lets you query collections with SQL-like syntax directly in C#. It works on any type that implements IEnumerable<T>.
slides.exampleOutput: A sequence of the even numbers.

exercise.prompt: LINQ queries operate on types that implement:

slides.title: Query Syntax vs Method Syntax
slides.content: LINQ has two styles: method syntax (numbers.Where(...)) and query syntax (from n in numbers where ... select n). Both compile to the same code.
slides.exampleOutput: a and b produce the same result.

exercise.prompt: Complete the query-syntax clause that filters items.

slides.title: Filtering with Where
slides.content: Where keeps elements that match a condition (a lambda returning bool). It does not change the originals — it returns a new sequence.

exercise.prompt: Complete the code to count words longer than 3 characters.
hints: The lambda takes each word (w) and returns true when it should be kept.
Compare w.Length to 3, keeping only longer words.

slides.title: Transforming with Select
slides.content: Select projects each element to a new shape (e.g. to uppercase, or to a single field). It returns one output element per input element.
slides.exampleOutput: An uppercase version of each word.

exercise.prompt: If Select is applied to a list of 5 elements, the result contains:

slides.title: Common LINQ Methods
slides.content: First/FirstOrDefault returns one item; OrderBy sorts; Distinct removes duplicates; Any/All test conditions; Count sums. They chain together fluently.
slides.example:
var best = words.OrderBy(w => w.Length).FirstOrDefault();
var anyLong = words.Any(w => w.Length > 3);

exercise.prompt: The method that returns true if at least one element matches is _____ (lambda).

slides.title: Chaining and Deferred Execution
slides.content: LINQ uses deferred execution: the query runs only when you enumerate it. Chaining methods returns IEnumerables you can keep combining until you finally consume them.
slides.exampleOutput: Materializes a sorted, uppercase list of long words.

exercise.prompt: Complete the chain so it returns a List of uppercase 4+ char words.
hints: You need Where (filter), Select (project), then a call that builds the List.
The final method is ToList(), which forces the query to run.
